items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: Frank Borowski brought in something he’d done for Doc Severinsen that Doc hated, called “Dichotomy.” ... But “Ayo,” A-Y-O, the one Wayne Andre did, Doc hated. So I featured Danny on that, and it went — but see I made a critical artistic error... I had a chart by Bill Berry on “Show,” Frank Borowski

ctx.x: Well he’s pretty astute to do something like that.

Yeah. But you see the combination of those things, when I put together my big band in fact I drew on some of the charts from “The Dick Cavett Show” to help me get the ensemble ready and I took some of the stuff from Lew Anderson’s band. I had this chart that he’d written for me on “Summer of ‘42” for me and Danny Stiles to play on and “My One and Only Love” was another feature. So I had those two plus a couple of other things and by the time I turned around I had maybe around I guess 12 or 13 charts that I could…

that some of the rock & roll lovers would buy the album just by the title alone, which they didn’t do of course, it didn’t fool anybody. But we put that on the fire and went around. And oddly enough it made enough noise so that all of a sudden I wound up winning a Down Beat poll that year and every other year for the next seven years, just on the strength of that alone, which tells you something about those polls. It’s basically a popularity contest. Because I play better now than I did back then and I don’t…
